ar_proposals._legal_warning: On a UAE trade licence the Arabic name is the LEGAL identifier, and DED/GBP listings should match the licence exactly. Whatever is already printed on the trade licence overrides every option below. Check the licence before choosing.

option_1_translation.note: Standard UAE trade-name construction (X for Y). Reads naturally to an Arabic speaker and is self-describing, which helps Arabic local search.

option_2_transliteration.means: phonetic rendering of the English name; carries no meaning in Arabic
option_2_transliteration.note: Matches the English brand sound exactly. Preferred if the brand is marketed in English and you want one spoken name.

option_3_hybrid.means: Emirates for Electric Scooters, keeping 'Emirates' transliterated
option_3_hybrid.note: Keeps brand recognition while staying descriptive.

ar_proposals.recommendation_reasoning: Google matches Arabic queries semantically, so a descriptive Arabic name ('electric scooters') earns relevance for Arabic searches like 'سكوتر كهربائي دبي' that a pure transliteration cannot. It is also the conventional form for a UAE retail trade name.
risks_to_check_before_filing: UAE trade-name rules restrict names of countries/emirates. 'الإمارات' may require approval or be refused by DED. Verify with the licensing authority.
'Emirates' is a heavily used mark in the UAE (Emirates airline group). Confirm there is no objection for this activity.
Confirm the Arabic name on the existing trade licence first - if one exists, use it verbatim and discard these options.
